comments.content: - `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.h:243` — The three methods are declared `static` with `(App::DocumentObject*, std::string)`, but their definitions at `DrawViewPart.cpp:1503`, `1514`, and `1524` are non-static one-argument members. Building `DrawViewPart.cpp` therefore fails with “no declaration matches” errors for all three definitions.

**DEFECT 1: Signature mismatch — header declaration does not match implementation**

**File:** `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.h` (lines at `+239`) vs `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.cpp` (lines at `+1498`)

The header declares all three functions as **static** with **two parameters** (`App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element`), but the implementations are **non-static** member functions with **one parameter** (`std::string element`).

Header (DrawViewPart.h):
```cpp
static bool isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
static bool isCosmeticEdge(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
static bool isCenterLine(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
```

Implementation (DrawViewPart.cpp):
```cpp
bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string element)  // non-static, one param
bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticEdge(std::string element)     // non-static, one param
bool DrawViewPart::isCenterLine(std::string element)       // non-static, one param
```

**Failure scenario:** Any translation unit that `#include`s `DrawViewPart.h` will see the static two-parameter declarations. The linker then cannot find definitions matching that signature (only the non-static one-parameter definitions exist). This **will not compile/link**. Specifically, any call like `DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(someView, elementName)` — matching the header's static signature — will fail with an undefined reference. And any existing callers from `DrawUtil::isCosmeticVertex(owner, element)` that were updated to call `DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(owner, element)` will fail at compile time due to wrong arity.

The implementations clearly intend to be non-static member functions using `this` (they call `getProjVertexByIndex()` and `getEdge()` implicitly), but the header was not updated to match — the static keyword and `App::DocumentObject* owner` parameter were left in the declarations.**DEFECT 1: Declaration/definition signature mismatch in DrawViewPart**

**File: `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.h` (lines 242-244)**
**File: `src/Mod/TechDraw/App/DrawViewPart.cpp` (lines 1501, 1514, 1527)**

The header declares three methods as `static` with an `App::DocumentObject* owner` parameter:
```cpp
static bool isCosmeticVertex(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
static bool isCosmeticEdge(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
static bool isCenterLine(App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element);
```

But the `.cpp` defines them as non-static member functions **without** the `owner` parameter:
```cpp
bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string element)  // missing static, missing owner
bool DrawViewPart::isCosmeticEdge(std::string element)
bool DrawViewPart::isCenterLine(std::string element)
```

**Failure scenario:** Any compilation unit including `DrawViewPart.h` and calling these methods (e.g., `DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(obj, "Vertex1")`) will fail to link — the declared symbols don't match the defined symbols. The code will not compile/link.
